action_criteria.expected_evidence: Serum anti-GluN1 positive (1:20); sodium 133 mmol/L; thyroid function, thyroid antibodies, neuronal-surface and onconeural antibodies normal or negative; beta-hCG negative
action_criteria.label: Obtain the serum work-up (blood count, chemistry, thyroid function and antibodies, HIV, beta-hCG, serum anti-GluN1 cell-based assay read with the CSF)
action_criteria.rationale: Screens metabolic, infectious, toxic and thyroid causes of a first psychotic presentation and gives the serum anti-GluN1 result, which supports but cannot replace the CSF assay.

action_criteria.expected_evidence: Essentially normal MRI with non-specific punctate periventricular T2/FLAIR signal; normal hippocampi; no enhancement or restricted diffusion
action_criteria.label: Obtain contrast-enhanced brain MRI to exclude HSV encephalitis, structural lesions and overlapping demyelination; a normal MRI does not exclude anti-NMDAR encephalitis
action_criteria.rationale: Excludes HSV encephalitis, structural lesions and overlapping demyelination before LP; it is normal or non-specific in most patients and does not confirm the diagnosis.

action_criteria.expected_evidence: No pleocytosis, no oligoclonal bands, normal IgG index, HSV PCR negative, CSF anti-GluN1 IgG positive (1:10)
action_criteria.label: Analyze CSF for cells, protein and glucose, OCB/IgG index, HSV PCR and a cell-based IgG anti-GluN1 assay interpreted in parallel with serum
action_criteria.rationale: With a bland CSF and a near-normal MRI and EEG, the CSF cell-based anti-GluN1 assay is the test that establishes the diagnosis.

action_criteria.expected_evidence: Mild diffuse slowing with bifrontal FIRDA; no epileptiform discharges or extreme delta brush
action_criteria.label: Obtain EEG for encephalopathic and epileptiform abnormalities, explicitly assessing for extreme delta brush
action_criteria.rationale: An encephalopathic EEG separates an organic encephalopathy from a primary psychosis, and the staring episodes need an electrographic assessment.

action_criteria.expected_evidence: Left ovarian 2.6 cm mature cystic teratoma
action_criteria.label: Perform pelvic and abdominal ultrasound to screen for an ovarian teratoma
action_criteria.rationale: Young women carry the highest teratoma risk; tumor removal is part of first-line treatment.

action_criteria.expected_evidence: Seizure burden and evolution of the background over 24 hours or more
action_criteria.label: Escalate to continuous EEG monitoring to quantify seizure burden and detect non-convulsive seizures
action_criteria.rationale: Repeated vacant staring episodes of uncertain nature need to be captured on video-EEG to separate non-convulsive seizures from non-epileptic events.

action_criteria.label: Optionally check her sertraline and loratadine against the acute agents
action_criteria.rationale: Sertraline adds a sodium and QTc caution but no interaction that changes management.

action_criteria.expected_evidence: General published evidence on anti-NMDAR encephalitis diagnosis and immunotherapy

action_criteria.rationale: Background reading only: no diagnostic or management step of this case depends on it.

prohibited_recommendations: Do not give haloperidol or other high-potency D2 antagonists for agitation: patients with anti-NMDAR encephalitis are prone to severe extrapyramidal and neuroleptic-malignant-like reactions.
Do not delay immunotherapy while waiting for the anti-NMDAR antibody result when clinical probability is high: antibody turnaround can take 1 to 2 weeks and delay worsens outcome.
Do not attribute the presentation to a primary psychiatric disorder while seizures, dyskinesias, autonomic instability, an abnormal EEG or CSF inflammation remain unexplained.
Do not perform lumbar puncture without prior imaging in a patient with altered consciousness, focal signs, or new seizures: exclude mass effect first.
Do not interpret a negative serum anti-NMDAR antibody as ruling out the disease; the CSF assay is the gold standard and may be positive when serum is negative.
required_recommendations: Start IV acyclovir 10 mg/kg every 8 hours at presentation, and stop it once CSF HSV PCR is negative and the antibody diagnosis is established; repeat the PCR on a second CSF sample if the first LP was within 72 hours of onset and HSV encephalitis remains plausible.

Start first-line immunotherapy without waiting for the antibody result once infection is reasonably excluded: IV methylprednisolone 1 g daily for 5 days with IVIG 0.4 g/kg/day for 5 days (2 g/kg total) or plasma exchange (5 to 7 exchanges).
Arrange prompt surgical removal of the left ovarian teratoma (laparoscopic, ovary-sparing where feasible) as part of first-line treatment, with gynecology.
Monitor with continuous EEG for non-convulsive seizures while consciousness fluctuates or seizures persist.
Admit to a neurology ward with seizure precautions and continuous cardiac monitoring.

If there is no meaningful clinical improvement 10 to 14 days after first-line therapy, escalate to rituximab (375 mg/m² weekly for 4 doses or 1 g twice 2 weeks apart, after hepatitis B screening) and/or cyclophosphamide; discuss fertility preservation before cyclophosphamide.
Treat agitation and insomnia with benzodiazepines (lorazepam) first.
Neurology-led care with psychiatry for behavioral management; gynecology for the teratoma.

avoided_actions.rationale: Transthoracic echo is not indicated for anti-NMDAR encephalitis; it adds cost without informing diagnosis or management unless a discrete cardiac concern (e.g., new murmur, embolic stroke) coexists.
EMG/NCS plays no role in the diagnostic workup of anti-NMDAR encephalitis; it neither confirms the antibody-mediated CNS process nor distinguishes among the differential diagnoses.
Amyloid PET targets Alzheimer pathology and contributes no information to the diagnosis or treatment of autoimmune encephalitis in a young patient with subacute neuropsychiatric symptoms.

DaTscan evaluates nigrostriatal dopaminergic function and has no role in autoimmune encephalitis; the orofacial dyskinesias of anti-NMDAR encephalitis are antibody-mediated, not presynaptic dopaminergic.

differential.key_features: Afebrile; CSF HSV PCR negative with no pleocytosis; MRI without temporal signal, hemorrhage or restricted diffusion; CSF anti-GluN1 positive.

differential.diagnosis: Other antibody-mediated encephalitis (anti-LGI1, CASPR2, GABA-B, AMPA, DPPX)
differential.key_features: Serum neuronal-surface panel negative (LGI1, CASPR2, GABA-B, AMPA, DPPX) and onconeural antibodies negative.
Disorientation and cognitive impairment (MMSE estimated below 24), staring episodes, EEG slowing with FIRDA, CSF anti-GluN1 positive and an ovarian teratoma.
Urine drug screen and alcohol negative; sertraline at a stable dose for two years with no clonus, hyperreflexia or hyperthermia.

key_clinical_evidence: Ten days of insomnia, then paranoia, disorganized thinking, disorientation and vacant staring episodes three weeks after a febrile respiratory illness: one of the six Graus 2016 groups (behavior and cognition), so the probable criteria are not met.
CSF IgG anti-GluN1 positive (titer 1:10) on cell-based assay: definite anti-NMDAR encephalitis (Graus 2016), even though the CSF is otherwise bland; serum positive 1:20 is read with the CSF.
MRI is essentially normal; MRI is normal or non-specific in about two thirds and excludes HSV encephalitis and structural causes.
EEG shows mild diffuse slowing with FIRDA and no extreme delta brush; extreme delta brush, when present, supports but does not establish the diagnosis, and its absence excludes nothing.
Pelvic ultrasound shows a 2.6 cm left ovarian mature cystic teratoma: its removal is part of first-line treatment.
Earlier immunotherapy and tumor removal are associated with better outcome (Titulaer 2013).

red_herrings.correct_interpretation: A viral-like prodrome precedes about 70% of anti-NMDAR encephalitis; it does not establish viral encephalitis, which CSF PCR addresses.
red_herrings.data_point: Mild upper respiratory illness with low-grade fever three weeks before the neuropsychiatric syndrome.
red_herrings.intended_effect: Suggests a primary viral encephalitis (HSV) or post-viral psychosis; tempts the agent to commit to empiric antiviral therapy without pursuing autoimmune workup.

red_herrings.correct_interpretation: Disorientation, cognitive impairment, staring episodes and an abnormal EEG are red flags that mandate exclusion of anti-NMDAR encephalitis before accepting a psychiatric diagnosis; a well-controlled anxiety disorder does not explain them.
red_herrings.data_point: Acute psychiatric presentation (paranoia, disorganized thinking, bizarre behavior) in a young woman with treated generalized anxiety disorder and no prior psychosis.
red_herrings.intended_effect: Anchors the agent on a primary psychiatric diagnosis (first-episode psychosis, brief psychotic disorder) and delays neurologic workup.

red_herrings.correct_interpretation: Hyponatremia occurs in anti-NMDAR encephalitis but is more typical of anti-LGI1 encephalitis; it needs its own work-up and correction and does not point away from the diagnosis.
red_herrings.data_point: Mild hyponatremia (sodium 133 mmol/L) in a patient taking sertraline.
red_herrings.intended_effect: Tempts the agent toward a primary metabolic-encephalopathy framing (SIADH from another cause, dehydration, polydipsia) instead of recognizing SIADH as a known complication of NMDAR-E.

sequence_constraints.reason: Imaging before LP in a patient with seizures or altered consciousness; CT head is an acceptable alternative, so the constraint is soft.

csf.interpretation: Opening pressure 15 cmH2O. WBC 3 cells/mcL (96% lymphocytes, 4% monocytes), protein 38 mg/dL and glucose 62 mg/dL (CSF/serum ratio 0.67): no pleocytosis. No oligoclonal bands; IgG index 0.56 (normal). Gram stain: no organisms; culture: no growth at 48 hours. HSV, VZV and enterovirus PCR not detected. Anti-NMDA receptor (GluN1) IgG positive on cell-based assay, titer 1:10. Clinical correlation recommended.

special_tests.NMDAR_antibodies: Positive, titer 1:10 (cell-based assay, IgG anti-GluN1; reference laboratory, resulted day 5)

alternatives: Plasma exchange (5 to 7 exchanges) is an alternative to IVIG.
contraindications: Class warning: haloperidol and other high-potency dopamine D2 antagonists are associated with severe extrapyramidal and neuroleptic malignant-like reactions in anti-NMDA receptor encephalitis.
interactions: Sertraline (current) and hyponatremia: SSRIs can cause SIADH-type hyponatremia; monitor sodium.
Sertraline with high-dose corticosteroids: corticosteroids can cause mood change, insomnia or psychosis; monitor mental state.
Sertraline with lorazepam: no pharmacokinetic interaction; additive sedation.
Sertraline with ondansetron or other QT-prolonging drugs: small additive QTc risk; check the ECG before adding them.
Loratadine: no clinically relevant interaction with the acute agents.
Acyclovir IV: crystal nephropathy risk; maintain hydration and monitor creatinine.
IVIG: risk of renal impairment and thrombosis; ensure hydration and avoid rapid infusion rates.
High-dose methylprednisolone: hyperglycemia, hypertension and hypokalemia; monitor glucose and electrolytes.
general.summary: Sertraline and loratadine reviewed against the acute agents; SSRI-associated hyponatremia and steroid neuropsychiatric effects to monitor. Class cautions listed above.
warnings: Rituximab: screen for hepatitis B (HBsAg, anti-HBc) before the first dose.
Cyclophosphamide is gonadotoxic and teratogenic: discuss fertility preservation and contraception.
Penicillin allergy (rash): not relevant to the agents above.

results.finding: Definite anti-NMDAR encephalitis requires one or more of six major symptom groups and IgG anti-GluN1 antibodies, with CSF testing included; probable disease requires four groups (or three with a teratoma) of rapid onset plus an abnormal EEG or CSF pleocytosis or oligoclonal bands.
results.source: Graus F et al. Lancet Neurol 2016;15:391-404

results.finding: All patients had antibodies in CSF, whereas about 14% were negative in serum; CSF titers related more closely to outcome than serum titers.
results.source: Gresa-Arribas N et al. Lancet Neurol 2014;13:167-177

results.finding: 38% had a tumor, mostly ovarian teratoma; 53% improved within 4 weeks of first-line immunotherapy or tumor removal; second-line rituximab or cyclophosphamide after first-line failure was associated with better outcome; 81% had mRS 0-2 at 24 months.
results.source: Titulaer MJ et al. Lancet Neurol 2013;12:157-165

results.finding: Extreme delta brush was found in 7 of 23 adults with anti-NMDAR encephalitis and was associated with a more prolonged illness.

anti-NMDA receptor encephalitis diagnosi.summary: Published criteria and cohort data on anti-NMDA receptor encephalitis: definite diagnosis rests on CSF IgG anti-GluN1 antibodies; first-line immunotherapy and tumor removal are followed by second-line agents when there is no response.

No focal lesion, mass effect, restricted diffusion, or pathological enhancement. Normal appearance of the hippocampi bilaterally

metadata.difficulty_rationale: 5 required tools, 3 red herrings, subtype=P; a psychiatric-only presentation with near-normal MRI, CSF and EEG, in which the diagnosis rests on the CSF anti-GluN1 assay and the teratoma
metadata.difficulty_variant_description: 22-year-old woman with psychiatric prodrome only — no seizures, normal MRI, near-normal CSF. Classic diagnostic puzzle presentation of anti-NMDAR encephalitis masquerading as first-break psychosis.
metadata.revision_reason: Independent Reviewer 2 anti-NMDAR audit: tumor screening tailored by age/sex and moved out of lab payloads; paired serum/CSF anti-GluN1 reachable; routine EEG baseline with selected continuous escalation; blanket CAP CT, FDG-PET and blood cultures removed

patient.chief_complaint: Bizarre behavior, paranoia, and social withdrawal for one week

social_history.living_situation: Lives in college dormitory with roommate

patient.history_present_illness: A 22-year-old right-handed woman with a history of generalized anxiety disorder was brought to the emergency department by her parents and college roommate after approximately one week of increasingly abnormal behavior. Per her roommate, the patient had been isolating herself in her room, refusing to attend classes, and had become increasingly suspicious that her friends were 'watching her' and 'talking about her behind her back.' She began barricading her door at night. Her parents noted she had stopped returning phone calls for five days, which was very unusual for her. When her mother finally reached her, she was speaking in a disorganized, tangential manner and accused her mother of being 'an imposter.' The patient herself reports feeling 'weird' and describes difficulty sleeping for about ten days, with nights where she does not sleep at all despite feeling exhausted. She has had no witnessed seizures and denies any focal neurological symptoms. She denies visual or auditory hallucinations but appears internally preoccupied at times during the interview. She did have a mild upper respiratory illness with low-grade fever approximately three weeks prior, which resolved spontaneously. Her friends noted she was 'completely normal' before this started. She has no prior psychotic or mood episodes, and her anxiety has been well-controlled on sertraline for two years. There is no prior psychotic illness in the family. Vitals on arrival were notable for mild tachycardia.

neurological_exam.additional: No nuchal rigidity. Kernig and Brudzinski signs negative. No rash. No lymphadenopathy.
neurological_exam.coordination: Finger-nose-finger intact bilaterally. Heel-shin not tested due to cooperation.
neurological_exam.cranial_nerves: Pupils equal and reactive to light bilaterally, 4mm. Extraocular movements intact without nystagmus. Face symmetric. Tongue midline. No orofacial dyskinesias observed on this examination.
neurological_exam.gait: Able to ambulate independently with normal gait.
neurological_exam.mental_status: Alert but disoriented to date (states it is 'last year'). Speech is tangential with loosening of associations. Makes eye contact inconsistently. Intermittent vacant staring episodes lasting 5-10 seconds with no clear responsiveness. No frank hallucinations elicited on direct questioning. MMSE not fully administered due to cooperation; estimated <24/30. Clock drawing disorganized.
neurological_exam.motor: Normal bulk and tone bilaterally. Full strength 5/5 in all extremities. No drift on outstretched arms.
neurological_exam.reflexes: Biceps, triceps, brachioradialis 2+ bilaterally. Patellar and Achilles 2+ bilaterally. Plantar response flexor bilaterally.
neurological_exam.sensory: Grossly intact to light touch in all extremities. Could not reliably complete full sensory exam due to limited cooperation.
